title: Transporting Schema
strapline: Everything must be moved from here to there — bags packed, baskets hauled, pockets stuffed. This is a schema, not a mess.
intent: Recognise transporting as a genuine line of enquiry — a toddler driven to carry objects, and themselves, from one place to another.
Understand the learning inside it: quantity, weight, distance, capacity and the sheer effort of moving a load.
Reframe the emptied shelf and the far-flung toys as research, so we resource the urge rather than fight it.
Build strength, coordination and spatial awareness through loading, lifting, pushing, pulling and unloading.
Feed the child's growing sense of purpose — 'I am taking these there because I have a plan'.
implementation: Give the transporter the right kit: bags, baskets, buckets, trolleys, prams, wheelbarrows, wagons and lots of loose, safely-sized things to move.
Set up destinations and journeys — a shop to carry to, a building site to deliver to, a home corner to stock.
Name the schema as you play alongside ('you're taking all the blocks over there — that's a heavy load!').
Watch where they carry to and resource it — if pinecones always end up in the mud kitchen, put a basket there for them.
Keep loads and containers safe, and reframe tidy-up as the ultimate transporting job — everything carried home.
key_questions: Where are you taking all of these?
Is your bag getting heavy — how will you carry it?
Which shall you move first, the big one or the little one?
How many can the wheelbarrow hold at once?
You've carried them all the way over there — what happens next?

impact.text: Toddlers push, pull and carry heavy loads on purpose, hauling bags and barrows from place to place.
Children fill containers, transport them and empty them elsewhere, running the whole cycle again and again.
Transporting turns social — a toddler delivers a load to a friend, packing and passing alongside them.
Early quantity words come with the load — 'more', 'all gone', 'big one', 'too heavy'.

enhancements: A fleet of transport — prams, wagons, wheelbarrows, shopping trolleys, dumper trucks.
A delivery role-play: a shop at one end, homes at the other, and parcels to carry between.
Bags of every kind — drawstring, handled, backpacks — for pockets that must be filled.
Guttering and pipes to transport water and balls from one point to another.
A tidy-up 'removal van' so packing everything away becomes the day's biggest job.

playing_exploring: The child pursues their own transporting agenda, moving what they choose to where they choose.
Loading and hauling engage the whole body in self-directed effort.
active_learning: Toddlers persist at heavy, awkward loads, refining how they carry to get the job done.
creating_thinking: Children form a plan — these there, those here — and follow it through, adjusting when a load is too big.
